requirements.text: WHEN a ticket is created with external refs, the system shall persist the ordered instance-scoped refs with that ticket's unchanged local identity.
WHEN a ticket or its metadata is read through a supported consumer, the system shall expose its stored refs without discarding unsupported or unconfigured reference strings.
WHEN attributes or content unrelated to refs are edited, the system shall preserve the stored external reference strings and their order.
WHEN a stored ref resolves against its explicitly named configured tracker instance, the system shall expose the issue URL built from that instance's configuration and the actual external identifier.
IF a stored ref cannot resolve safely, THEN the system shall retain its searchable text and expose an unavailable result without a navigable destination.
WHEN external references are displayed on a ticket card, the system shall show a tracker icon, the actual external key, and an external-navigation arrow for each resolved inline reference.
WHEN a user activates a resolved reference link, the system shall open that external issue in a new tab without also opening or dragging the parent ticket card.
WHEN a user requests reference details, the system shall expose every full reference identity and any unavailable reason without requiring external navigation.
WHEN tickets are filtered by free text, the system shall include matches against stored external refs alongside the existing searchable fields.

WHEN Quick Search receives an external identifier that also has a local-ticket-key shape, the system shall return the eligible local-key and external-reference matches together with their match provenance.
WHEN Quick Search returns matching tickets, the system shall deduplicate by local project-and-ticket identity and rank exact identifier matches above partial external matches.
WHEN a query has only a fuzzy or partial external identifier match, the system shall require explicit result selection rather than automatically opening that match.
WHEN a ticket's complete references are viewed or edited, the system shall expose that full list independently of board badge-visibility preferences.
The system shall keep tracker instances distinct even when their tracker kinds and external identifiers are equal.
The system shall preserve configured base-URL context paths and encode external identifier data so it cannot alter the intended URL structure.
The system shall support canonical GitHub owner/repository and GitLab subgroup namespace issue references while excluding GitLab merge-request inference.
The system shall preserve existing behavior for tickets without refs and projects without tracker configuration.
The system shall provide keyboard-visible focus, announced new-tab links, and actual interactive target sizes of at least 24 pixels with text of at least 11 pixels for external-reference controls.
The system shall preserve unrelated existing board badge preferences when introducing external-reference visibility.
The system shall preserve unknown tracker configuration and unsupported ref text through unrelated configuration or ticket mutations.
The system shall use explicit stored refs as the sole external identity source rather than deriving tracker destinations from local ticket numbering.
The system shall perform external reference linking and search without calling external tracker APIs or introducing synchronization.
The system shall resolve only credential-free HTTP(S) issue URLs on the explicitly configured tracker's base origin without unresolved template placeholders.

The system shall expand repository-relative shorthand into stored identity only for newly supplied replacement or add operands when that explicitly named instance has a default repository, never during reads or configuration changes.
IF an optional tracker entry is invalid or unsupported, THEN the system shall keep the local project available and expose the affected refs as unavailable with a diagnostic.

WHEN refs are replaced, added, removed, or cleared through supported mutation interfaces, the system shall apply ordered and idempotent changes by normalizing supplied replacement/add operands, removing only exact stored strings, and preserving untouched strings and their order.
WHEN a ref removal operand is supplied, the system shall remove only exact stored-string matches without expanding or rebinding that operand.

The system shall preserve stored external identifiers and URL identities without local MDT code limits, number padding or local relationship-key normalization while permitting configured display-only shortening.
WHEN external reference display shortening is configured, the system shall render context-aware abbreviated labels while retaining full stored identifiers, destinations and inspectable identities.

WHEN Quick Search displays a local ticket with external refs, the system shall display external-reference badges independently of board badge-visibility settings, including for results matched by local identity or title.

WHEN a user searches an issue number without a prefix, the system shall include matching local and external issue numbers, while a #number query selects only complete matching external repository-issue numbers rather than local/Jira-only identities or longer numbers.

scenarios.title: Create and read stored external references
scenarios.given: a local project and external refs work:PROJ-123 and gh:acme/widgets#42
scenarios.when: I create a local ticket with those refs and then read its details and metadata
scenarios.then: the local ticket keeps its allocated MDT key and exposes both stored refs in their original order

scenarios.title: Compose explicit reference changes
scenarios.given: a ticket with refs work:PROJ-123 and legacy:OPS-7
scenarios.when: I add gh:acme/widgets#42 twice, remove work:PROJ-123 twice, then replace refs with an empty list
scenarios.then: duplicate adds and absent removals are no-ops and the explicit empty replacement clears the ticket's refs

scenarios.title: Preserve unsupported refs through unrelated changes
scenarios.given: a ticket with supported, unknown-instance and unsupported external refs
scenarios.when: I edit its status and then its Markdown content without editing refs
scenarios.then: all ref strings and their order survive both writes and subsequent detail and metadata reads

scenarios.title: Inspect complete references and unavailable reasons
scenarios.given: a ticket card with one, two, or several refs including a long identifier or unavailable tracker
scenarios.when: I open its reference details using touch or keyboard
scenarios.then: the complete list exposes full identifiers, configured instance names, and unavailable reasons without navigating to an external tracker

scenarios.title: Retain external navigation in read-only viewing
scenarios.given: a read-only local ticket card with a configured external ref
scenarios.when: I activate its external issue link
scenarios.then: the correct external issue opens in a new tab while local editing and dragging remain unavailable

scenarios.title: Return both local and external exact key matches
scenarios.given: one ticket whose local key matches PROJ-123 and other local tickets storing external identifier PROJ-123, including one with both identities
scenarios.when: I search for PROJ-123 in Quick Search
scenarios.then: all eligible exact matches are shown with local/external provenance, each local ticket appears once, and partial external matches rank below exact matches

scenarios.title: Require selection for partial external matches
scenarios.given: a query matching only part of one stored external identifier
scenarios.when: I search for that text without choosing a result
scenarios.then: the matching local ticket is listed but does not automatically open

scenarios.title: refs open correct instance
scenarios.given: a visible ticket card with configured Jira project PRJ and repository acme/widgets refs
scenarios.when: I inspect the shortened icon-and-key badges and activate a chosen reference
scenarios.then: only configured matching context is shortened, full identities remain inspectable, and the correct actual issue opens in a new tab without opening or dragging the local ticket

scenarios.title: refs board filter
scenarios.given: tickets with local number 123, Jira key PRJ-123, repository issue acme/widgets#123, and unknown-instance repository refs
scenarios.then: 123 finds matching local and external tickets while #123 finds repository issue number 123 only, including unconfigured repository refs, and does not match #1234 or Jira/local-only identities

scenarios.title: refs viewer independent visibility
scenarios.given: a ticket with refs whose board reference badges are hidden
scenarios.when: I search by that ticket's title or local identity, open the viewer and explicitly replace its reference list
scenarios.then: the search result always shows its external badges and the complete viewer list remains readable/editable independently of the board preference
